A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELM/ELM-MIL research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original EEG-language pretraining, retrieval, classification on TUAB, NMT, TUSZ and TUEV, and multiple ablation analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds LaBraM linear-probe comparisons and temporal-alignment case studies.

M1.justification: The ELM variants, encoders, projection strategies, and bidirectional MIL alignment procedure are retained. v4 refines normalization documentation and task-specific sampling configurations, without establishing a newly introduced algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining data, retrieval population, and TUAB, NMT, TUSZ and TUEV classification tasks. The added alignment illustrations examine existing hold-out recordings; no additional dataset or evaluated clinical task is introduced.

E2.justification: LaBraM-Base, already represented by published fine-tuning results in Table 4, is newly evaluated using the authors’ linear-probing pipeline on NMT, TUAB and TUEV in v4 Appendix A.1. The existing EEG-only comparators remain; SV is merely renamed Supervised.

E3.justification: v4 adds frozen-LaBraM linear-probing protocols and specifies M=24 sentence segments for five-second tasks, replacing v3’s general M=8 paragraph specification; N=120 was already reported. These are reported configuration changes, without establishing reruns. v4 Table 9 labels TUEV as 80% labeled, versus 100% in Table 6, without explaining whether the percentages use different denominators.

E4.justification: v4 Section 4.2.4 and Appendix E.3 add temporal-alignment case studies comparing report-snippet similarity with corresponding EEG crops, including successful, failed and normal-recording examples. Existing aggregation, sampling, temperature, shuffled-report, per-class, leakage and prompt analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 Appendix A.1 explicitly describes five repetitions of 10-fold cross-validation, reusing one pretrained LaBraM checkpoint while varying ELM-MIL pretraining initialization across repetitions. This distinguishes the variability represented by the new comparison’s standard deviations. Existing uncertainty-reporting conventions remain.

E6.justification: New LaBraM results, balanced-accuracy entries and alignment findings supplement unchanged main results. For example, v4 Table 7 adds NMT 100%-label LaBraM AUROC 82.02 against the retained ELM-MIL 89.77. However, new Table 8 gives ELM-MIL TUAB 10%/100% AUROCs of 91.91/93.14, conflicting with 93.14/93.91 in both versions’ Table 2; these cannot establish verified performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 states the squared-distance/dot-product identity using unqualified embeddings. v4 Equations 4–6 explicitly use normalized EEG/text embeddings and specify normalization before and after projection, supplying a missing condition for that identity. This is a localized mathematical specification correction; the remaining formalism is retained.

C1.justification: The central novelty, retrieval, zero-shot and label-efficiency claims remain. v4’s Discussion additionally positions pathology-sensitive alignment as a critical step toward automated report generation, extending its claimed prospective contribution without reporting a generation system.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new examples as temporally selective alignment without temporal labels. Figure 16 links failed localization to subtle slowing and rarely described frontotemporal spikes. The new Impact Statement also discusses event-frequency dependence, channel-specific attribution, language-model bias and future documentation applications.

D1.justification: v4 adds a repository location for code and pretrained models in the Discussion and makes normalization and task-specific text sampling more explicit. Hardware, software versions, optimizer settings and training-time information were already present. Repository availability is asserted by the PDF and was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v4 adds subject-identity EEG pretraining work by Gijsen and Ritter, five works on general vision-language learning, and Biswal et al.’s report auto-completion work. These modestly broaden research positioning; the principal related-work categories and existing references remain.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper, introduces clinical-phenotyping terminology, separates Methods from Experimental Setup, consolidates pretraining settings, and adds an Impact Statement. Most existing prose and appendix explanations remain closely matched, limiting the extent of rewriting.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the visual presentation with three comparison tables and five multipanel alignment figures combining similarity curves with EEG traces. It also adopts ICML title, abstract and header formatting and relocates existing displays. All thirteen v3 figures are retained without redrawing.

improvement.justification: The added direct LaBraM comparisons, temporal-alignment successes and failures, clearer technical specification, and code/model access information strengthen comparative support, interpretability and reproducibility. These are incremental gains over an already extensive evaluation. The new TUAB Table 8 conflicts with retained Table 2 values, tempering confidence in part of the added evidence.
